the Winsor & Newman (W&N), the largest pigment manufacturer in the world, manufactured three different chromate yellow formulations in the late 19th and early 20th century.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of three 19th century chromate pigments: barium, zinc potassium and strontium chromites.

the identification of these yellow chromate pigmentation systems and their use in 19th and 20th century Portuguese artworks, as a means to better understand and interpret the changes that may have taken place on their chromatic and optical properties over time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 19th–20th century W&Ns Lemon Yellow (BaCrO42H2O), Citron Yellow (4Zn2O3·Cr2O3·3H2) and Strontian (SrCrO42H) pigments were manufactured by the addition of the appropriate metal oxides to a solution of sodium chromate (Na2CrO4), followed by a precipitation step.
W&N produced barium, zinc and, to a lesser extent, strontium chromatic pigments in the 19th and early 20th centuries.
the 19th and early 20th century chromate yellows based on barium, zinc and/or strontium were not manufactured in the same manner, contrary to the chromate yellow based on lead (PbCr4+).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the W&N archive database has provided an invaluable insight into the manufacture of 19th century barium, zinc and potassium chromate pigments, and the complementary analytical techniques have allowed their identification in historic paintings.
the TS of the 19 cent. yellow chromates pigments is lower than the TS of the PbCrO4, and the use of extenders was probably not to reduce the cost of these pigments.

the 19th and early 20th century chromate pigments were manufactured in a more controlled manner than their 20th century counterparts, with a clear distinction in the production methods of barium, zinc and calcium chromate yellow pigments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TS is not the only parameter to take into account when considering the addition of extenders to a pigment formulation.
